sites.n: 31st Navy Arsenal explosions, Ulyanovsk (Zavolzhsky district)
cas: Deaths: 2 (servicemen I. Kuznetsov and V. Pankov); a second blast on 23 Nov 2009 killed 8 more
Injured: 7 (MChS 2015); 10 (MChS report to the President, 14 Nov 2009); 60 (Kremlin, 24 Nov 2009)
Evacuated: more than 1,000 placed in temporary accommodation; military town of about 3,000 (625 children) in the danger zone
sites.kf: At 15:44 a fire in an ammunition-disposal workshop of FGUP '31st Arsenal of the Navy' (Russian MoD) set off a series of explosions of stored munitions. The fire covered more than 100,000 m2, was localized at 17:30 and declared extinguished at 22:55 MSK. 2,319 personnel and 251 vehicles responded; the emergency regime was lifted on 25 Dec 2009; damage was put at 227 million roubles. The Kremlin attributed the fire preliminarily to a violation of disposal technology. On 23 Nov 2009, while unexploded munitions were being loaded, a shell detonated and set off munitions in a vehicle, killing two officers and six contract servicemen.

sites.n: Vozrozhdeniya Island Soviet biological-weapons test site (Aral Sea)
sites.ty: former BW open-air test site and anthrax burial pits
sites.st: former; burial pits targeted by US CTR decontamination plan (2001-2002)
sites.kf: The DoD point paper (Jan 2002) describes 11 side-by-side unlined burial pits, each about 4 ft wide, 10 ft long and 4-6 ft deep, reportedly containing weaponized anthrax believed to come from the BW facility at Yekaterinburg (formerly Sverdlovsk). In Oct 1997 a US team took 64 pit samples, 36 from laboratory buildings and 110 from around the test facility; about 11 of the 64 pit samples tested positive for live anthrax spores, and one building sample for plague. The CTR plan aimed to decontaminate the pits and demolish all buildings.

sites.n: Baikonur Proton-M launch failure and heptyl contamination
sites.ty: rocket crash on the cosmodrome (Russian-leased territory)
sites.kf: A Proton-M with a DM-03 upper stage and three Glonass-M satellites, launched on 2 Jul 2013, fell and exploded about ten seconds after launch between pads 81 and 200 on territory leased by Russia. Kazakhstan's Environment Minister said that heptyl (UDMH) above the permitted concentration was not found in air or soil in the surrounding villages. Kazcosmos said in Sep 2013 that detoxification was complete: 'heptyl content in the soil was reduced from 8850 MPC to the level of 952. Now there is a normal level of heptyl - about 1 MPC'.

sites.n: Listvyazhnaya coal mine methane disaster (Kuzbass)
sites.kf: 285 miners were underground and 239 were brought out (MChS). Rostekhnadzor's technical investigation (closed 14 Sep 2022) found the main technical causes to be gas build-up in the longwall from insufficient air, electrical equipment running in an explosive atmosphere, and hardware/software tampering with the gas-monitoring system. Organizational causes were systematic falsification of ventilation-safety readings, ignoring personal gas detectors, and people working in gassed workings. The materials were passed to the Investigative Committee.

sites.n: Kostenko coal mine fire and methane explosion (ArcelorMittal Temirtau)
sites.ty: underground coal mine · Operator: ArcelorMittal Temirtau JSC (at the time)
sites.kf: 252 miners were underground and 205 were lifted to safety. A Government Commission chaired by PM A. Smailov was formed the same day; the government also moved to complete the transfer of the enterprise to the Republic of Kazakhstan. The commission's final sitting (9 Dec 2023) found the employer 100% liable: gas ignition caused the fire and the subsequent methane explosion, with negligent upkeep and inspection. 19 people were found responsible for safety-rule violations, and the results went to law enforcement.

sites.n: Mailuu-Suu uranium legacy site (tailings and waste-rock dumps)
sites.ty: Soviet uranium mining/milling legacy: 23 tailings locations · Operator: state (legacy); remediation under EBRD ERA
sites.kf: More than 2 million m3 of tailings lie at 23 locations (almost 50 ha) along the Mailuu-Suu River and its tributaries in a seismically active area, with some houses less than 500 m away; a landslide occurred in 2019 (IAEA SMP). The ERA project covers 39 waste-rock dumps, 16 tailings ponds, 6 shafts and 49 adits; clean-up was underway as of the EBRD page. Under the World Bank project, tailings pond No. 3 was relocated to No. 6 (project completed March 2017, Kyrgyz presentation).

sites.n: Min-Kush uranium legacy site
sites.ty: uranium mines, waste-rock piles and tailings dams (Tuyuk-Suu, Taldy-Bulak, Kak, Dalnee) · Operator: state (legacy)
sites.kf: About 130 km south of Bishkek on the Min-Kush River (a Syr-Darya tributary). Four closed mines and tailings dams hold about 1.9 million m3 of uranium tailings; mining ceased in the late 1960s. The ERA scope was 24 waste-rock dumps (about 13.5 ha, 0.9 million m3) and mine openings; the CIS programme covered the tailings. Remediated (one of the four ERA sites completed by 2025).
